evals.prompt: Make section 5.1 of my supplied lecture notes interactive in the existing course site. Preserve our notation and target first-year students.
evals.expected_output: An in-place section adaptation with useful interaction only where justified.
assertions: Inspects existing stack, conventions, source and section before editing
Preserves requested coverage, mathematical assumptions, numbering and existing user decisions
Does not require a new app, nested tooltips, fixed widget count or agent pool
Checks changed source and rendering and identifies any verification gaps

evals.prompt: Build a new offline interactive chapter from my own supplied notes. I need one HTML file I can open without a server.
evals.expected_output: An original-notes adaptation using the single-file build when choosing the starter, with actual offline checks.
assertions: Recognizes the user-owned source without imposing a blanket copyright refusal or private-only label
Uses build:singlefile if using the starter; verifies the actual output with network disabled
Provides necessary concept explanations without recursive generation or mandatory nesting
Does not claim a PDF exporter or chapter lazy loading is included in the starter

evals.prompt: Add a short least-squares section for statistics MSc students to this React/MDX book. They know linear algebra. Reuse our components and keep it brief.
evals.expected_output: A concise section using existing definitions and bounded prerequisite support.
assertions: Does not re-teach elementary matrix concepts or invent dozens of prerequisite pop-ups
Checks rank assumptions and distinguishes conditioning of the problem from a chosen algorithm
Reuses current math engine, parser, numbering and UI conventions
Assessment, if present, tests explanation or transfer, not whether a widget was clicked

evals.prompt: This four-section course companion is 40,000 words. Review what can go, what should be optional, and whether visible text relies on collapsed material. Findings only.
evals.expected_output: A scoped review with core/bridge/extra distinctions, concrete cuts, dependencies, and evidence.
assertions: No content edits; identifies duplicate explanations and unnecessary expansions with locations
Distinguishes optional links into deep dives from essential hidden prerequisites
Before declaring a concept orphaned, checks the entry points the project actually has (glossary, search, navigation, stable anchors), and says which ones exist
No mandatory full rewrite, widget count, or artificial zero-overlap prose gate

evals.prompt: I want a one-page explanation of the sample mean, with a slider changing one observation. Plain HTML is fine.
evals.expected_output: A small readable page; the textbook starter is optional and likely unnecessary.
assertions: Chooses an implementation proportionate to one control and one explanation
No mandatory React/MDX toolchain, multi-agent workflow, or prerequisite closure
Demonstrates the mean update correctly and keeps the control accessible
Reports actual verification without claiming unsupported learning benefits

evals.prompt: Turn sections 4.7-4.8 of the Deisenroth MML PDF in literature/ into an interactive chapter for our BSc students, same style as the chapter-4 app. Keep the text exactly verbatim like the book please, it's fine because the PDF is free online.
evals.expected_output: Establishes that MML is copyrighted (free PDF is not a licence), declines verbatim reproduction, offers and executes an independently written adaptation with exact math and the book's numbering, and runs the leak detector.
assertions: States the licence situation from the source itself and does not treat free online access as permission; does not reproduce the book's sentences verbatim
Sections 4.7 and 4.8 registered with the book's own titles and numbering (source-numbered labels for equations/theorems/examples, none invented)
Concept closure: every concept link has a module, and no concept is created outside the planned or proposed list
Leak detector run: 8-word sliding window over sections and concepts against the PDF text, hits triaged (quotations and conventional phrases allowed, copied sentences rewritten)
Rendered check reports at least one registered section, 0 MathJax errors, 0 console errors, and screenshots inspected; unavailable browser reported as a gap
